data.body:
Operator 2026-10-22 (verbatim): "The goal is to keep consistency between ID generated by different agents for the same project". Operator answered "Yes, create P-id-consistency (Recommended)": one phase with waves: allocation test and conformance lint first, then phase prefixes and templates for new kinds, then vocabulary aliases and presets; held behind the org layer where it needs it.

EVIDENCE (measured on this project's log, see the conformance-lint task): 836 bugs, of which 677 carry the machine form B<hash> and 159 are agent-chosen slugs (B-ci-gate-prints-passed-with-failing-tests...); 464 fix tasks, of which 385 are fix-B<hash> and 79 are fix-B-<slug>; task ids use dozens of ad-hoc prefixes (US-, RQM-, SPEC-, PI-, ACF-, LS-, SU-, B-uni, P-agent..., fix-B...). Cause: --id / caller-named ids let every agent invent a shape.

GOVERNING RECORDS: decision D-id-schemes-final (templates per kind defaulting to today's ids, {seq} keys, one namespace with a taken-key check, vocabulary aliases); research Rb1695227af; built already: B-id-config ([ids] templates), B-id-generator (id service). Org-wide conventions arrive through B-org-layers.

WAVES: 1 allocation proof + conformance lint (and ID-decide, the operator questions); 2 phase prefix registry, templates for new kinds, templates for tasks/phases; 3 vocabulary aliases and presets (needs B-org-layers), end-to-end transcript test; 4 docs.
data.title: Id consistency: ids minted by different agents for one project follow one convention (allocation, conformance, phase prefixes, templates, vocabulary presets)

data.body:
The id service (B-id-generator, done) allocates {seq} keys with a taken-key check. Two agents in parallel worktrees or two clones can still pick the same next number. Write a test with N concurrent processes minting from separate worktrees (log shards merge by event) and a two-clone merge: the second mint gets a suffix or is CONTESTED per D-id-schemes-final, never a silent duplicate; add a 'ddflow doctor' check for duplicate keys. Fix what the test finds (file bugs).

Moved from the loose task DX-id-concurrent-allocation-test into phase P-id-consistency (a task cannot be re-parented); DX-id-concurrent-allocation-test is abandoned with a pointer here.
data.title: Prove {seq} and next-free allocation is collision-free across agents, worktrees and clones

data.body:
Operator 2026-10-22: the goal is CONSISTENCY between ids generated by different agents for the same project. Measured on this log (836 bugs, 464 fix tasks): 677 bug ids are the machine form B<hash> but 159 are agent-chosen slugs (B-ci-gate-prints-passed-with-failing-tests...), 385 fix tasks are fix-B<hash> but 79 are fix-B-<slug>; task ids use dozens of ad-hoc prefixes. Cause: --id lets every agent invent a shape. Add [ids].enforce = off|warn|refuse (default warn): a caller-supplied id for a machine-minted kind (bug, lesson, research, decision, memory, job, fix task) must match the pattern derived from its template, else it is minted instead or refused with the right form; an explicit slug stays allowed only where the template says caller-named. 'ddflow doctor' lists nonconforming existing ids (they are never renamed: recorded ids are immutable). Tests: warn, refuse, minted fallback, doctor.

Moved from the loose task DX-id-conformance-lint into phase P-id-consistency (a task cannot be re-parented); DX-id-conformance-lint is abandoned with a pointer here.
data.title: Id conformance: an explicit id must match its kind's [ids] template (warn/refuse by knob), ddflow doctor lists existing nonconforming ids

data.body:
Tasks and phases are caller-named (D-id-schemes-final covers imported ones only), so parallel agents pick different shapes (US-, RQM-, SPEC-, PI-, ACF-, LS-, SU- were each chosen by the researching agent; older phases use B-uni, P-agent..., fix-B...). Add an optional 'id_prefix' on a phase (set by phase add, a preset, or the org vocabulary) and have 'ddflow task add --phase P' with no id mint the next free <prefix>-<seq> through the id service (next_seq, taken-key check across worktrees), and with an explicit id warn or refuse a non-conforming prefix per [ids].enforce. Print the convention in the claim/brief charter so agents follow it, and in 'ddflow plan check' (warn on a plan whose task ids break the phase prefix). Org/company convention via the org layer (B-org-layers); presets via DX-id-vocabulary-aliases.

Moved from the loose task DX-id-phase-prefix-registry into phase P-id-consistency (a task cannot be re-parented); DX-id-phase-prefix-registry is abandoned with a pointer here.
data.title: Phase id prefixes: a phase declares the id prefix of its tasks; task add under it mints or validates PREFIX-<n>, and the agent charter states it

data.body:
The [ids] section has one template per existing kind (bug B{hash}, lesson, research, decision, memory, job, session, fix_task, promotion, ci_bug, split_child, imported_*). The kinds planned in P-requirements (requirement), P-user-stories (story, criterion, persona) and P-specs (spec) must register ID_PREFIXES and an [ids] default in the kind descriptor (record contract RC1-RC12) rather than invent ids: defaults e.g. REQ-{seq}, US-{seq}, AC-{story}-{seq}, SPEC-{seq}, readable and project-overridable; add a test that every registered record kind has an [ids] template and a doctor check. Needs the kinds registry.

data.body:
Tasks and phases are named by whoever adds them (ddflow task add <ID>); only imported ones use [ids] imported_phase/imported_task. Let a project set [ids] task = 'T-{seq}' / phase = 'P{seq}' (or a company convention like PROJ-{seq}) so 'task add' with no id mints the next free key via the id service (next_seq, taken-key check), keeping explicit ids working and the default 'caller names it'. Needs the id service B-id-generator (done). Cover CLI, MCP, prompt: the agent is told the convention in the charter.

data.body:
Operator 2026-10-22 asked for record id naming conventions configurable by config file, CLI, company policy or prompt with presets. D-id-schemes-final (2026-10-05) already decided 'vocabulary aliases commands and MCP tools' (user-visible names for kinds), but ddflow/services/vocabulary.py does not exist: only the [ids] templates (B-id-config, B-id-generator) are built. Build the alias layer: [vocabulary] kind -> display name/plural/prefix, accepted as command nouns and MCP action values, shown in output; layered (default < org < project < local) through the org-config stack (B-org-layers); presets (software, support-desk, research-lab) shipped as data.

data.body: Ask the operator (AskUserQuestion) and record each answer as a decision (ddflow decision add --globs ddflow/core/ids.py,ddflow/config_sections/ids.py, alternatives set). Goal (operator, verbatim): "The goal is to keep consistency between ID generated by different agents for the same project". Questions with RECOMMENDED defaults: (1) [ids].enforce default: warn (recommended) vs refuse vs off. (2) Phase id prefix registry: a phase declares id_prefix and task add under it mints PREFIX-<n> (recommended: yes, optional per phase). (3) Shipped presets: software, support-desk, research-lab (recommended). (4) Default templates for new kinds: requirement REQ-{seq}, story US-{seq}, criterion AC-{story}-{seq}, spec SPEC-{seq} (recommended). (5) Does --id stay allowed for machine-minted kinds (bug, lesson, research, decision, memory, job, fix task)? Recommended: allowed only when it matches the kind template (warn by default, refuse under enforce=refuse); caller-named kinds (task, phase) unchanged unless a template is set. Acceptance: decisions recorded; downstream tasks cite them; the decision-needing tasks read these answers before building.
data.title: Operator decisions for id consistency: enforce default, phase prefix registry, presets, default templates for new kinds, --id for machine-minted kinds

data.body: Goal (operator): "The goal is to keep consistency between ID generated by different agents for the same project". Script two agents (as_agent a and b) in parallel worktrees of one project with a configured [ids] and a phase id_prefix: each files bugs (bug found), tasks (task add with no id and with a non-conforming explicit id), and a phase, then the logs merge. Assert: every id conforms to its kind template or phase prefix (or carries the warn/refuse outcome), no duplicate keys across the merged log, doctor reports zero nonconforming ids for the new records, the transcript (commands and outputs) is kept as a golden. File any defect found as a bug.
data.title: End-to-end transcript test: two agents in parallel worktrees file bugs, tasks and a phase; every id conforms, none duplicate

data.body: Document how ids are formed per kind, the [ids].enforce knob (off|warn|refuse), phase id_prefix and task/phase templates, presets (software, support-desk, research-lab) and vocabulary aliases, org-layer overrides, and the rule for agents: never invent an id shape, let ddflow mint it or follow the phase prefix. Acceptance: docs check passes; examples are exercised by ID-e2e.
